newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian, Croatian companies sign $47m oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Albanian, Croatian companies sign $47m oil deal.

text.p: Albania's Albpetrol oil company and Croatia's INA Naftaplin signed a $47 million research and development contract on Wednesday.
Albanian television said INA would invest the sum in a research and development scheme in the event of striking oil in the jointly-operated Panaja field near Vlore, western Albania.
State-owned Albpetrol would invest $17 million in the scheme.
INA said it had found methane gas in a separate onshore well it had drilled to the depth of 1,700 metres at a site west of Tirana and hoped to strike oil early next year.
"We hope to strike oil at 5,500 metres depth. We plan to come to that point by around January or February next year," INA's Albania operations executive director Marjan Pecic said.
Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa, who ended a two-day visit to Albania, held talks with President Sali Berisha and Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi.
The two countries, which share an Adriatic coastline, agreed to develop cooperation in tourism, oil and gas exploration, and in the food and pharmaceutical industries.
